value.title: Mac knob guard: keep the knob with the ESP32
value.complexity_breakdown: S=1, I=1 (macOS Bluetooth via blueutil), D=0, N=1, F=1, T=1 = 5 → CS-3 by points; scoped as small

sections.name: summary
sections.value: macOS re-pairs the Anticater knob at times and steals it from the ESP32 bridge. A launchd job runs scripts/mac_knob_guard.sh every 10 s: if blueutil shows the knob (by address ee-aa-b8-d6-82-5e or an ANTICATER name) paired to the Mac, it disconnects and unpairs only that device and logs one JSON line; a failing blueutil query is logged as an error instead of silently doing nothing. just mac-guard-on/off/status.

sections.name: goals
value: The knob stays with the ESP32 without Vaughan disconnecting it on the Mac.
Never touch any other Bluetooth device.
Easy to turn off (rollback to the Mac daemon).

value.claim: When the knob is paired to the Mac, the guard disconnects and unpairs exactly that device and logs it (fake-blueutil test).
With no knob paired the guard is silent and changes nothing; a blueutil failure is logged as an error.
just mac-guard-on installs a launchd job (every 10 s, survives reboots) that runs cleanly; mac-guard-off stops and disables it.
value.receipt: mac-guard-on → launchd runs=2, last exit 0, no error lines

value.claim: Observed in real use: the knob no longer stays on the Mac (a guard.log unpair line when it happens).

value.question: Fix for the Mac re-grabbing the knob?
value.answer: Vaughan: "Build the guard (install blueutil)" (brew install blueutil approved).

value.mitigation: Disconnect first; unpair failures are logged as unpair_failed; guard retries every 10 s.
